newsitem.title: MEXICO: Nevada Goldfields plans Mexican expansion.
newsitem.headline: Nevada Goldfields plans Mexican expansion.

text.p: Denver-based Consolidated Nevada Goldfields Corp plans a massive expansion at its recently-acquired Pachuca silver mine in Mexico, the company's president and CEO said here Monday.
Geoffrey Hoyl told the Mexican Mining 1997 conference that the five year plan of the company was to boost output 300 percent and decrease costs per ounce by 34 percent.
"At the end of the day, we will be producing 6.7 million ounces (of silver) per year at Pachuca, which will make us one of the biggest producers in the hemisphere," Holy said.

He said silver output there in 1997 was expected to be 2.7 million ounces, rising to 3.8 million ounces in 1998 and reaching 5.3 million ounces in 1999. For gold, Hoyl said production would also gradually increase from 13,000 ounces in 1997, to 19,000 in 1998 and 27,000 in 1999.
Nevada Goldfields bought out mining company Grupo Real del Monte SA from closely-held Grupo Acerero del Norte in summer last year.

The acquisition included 116,000 acres at Pachuca, a copper and gold mine called El Baztan, the Magistral del Oro mine where the company will process tailings, the Barita de Sonora mine where 300,000 tonnes of barite are mined annually, half sold to the state-owned oil monopoly Pemex and the other half exported to Texas.
At El Baztan, Nevada Golfields has 110,000 acres under its control and Hoyl estimated output would produce 5 million pounds of copper at an average price of 47 cents (U.S.) per pound.

Hoyl said that also part of the five year plans are to improve mining methods and to bring in place new contracts with unions, to include production bonuses and also to extract water from mines to expose new mineralisations.
